market_holds: Spot 13.615 at the 18:08 UTC seal (Yahoo bars put it at 14.02 by 19:28 UTC). It is down 17% over 5 sessions, 40% over 20 and about 56% from 31.63 on 2026-10-07, 71% below the 52-week high and 2% above the low. 20-day realised vol is 104%. Front-expiry (Dec 18) straddle is 23.7%; the event share, net of ordinary vol, is 9.4%. 25-delta skew is +5.25 vol points toward puts. Sources: the sealed baseline and the Yahoo chart I fetched. Over the same stretch VNET fell about 64% and KWEB about 13%, so most of the fall belongs to the China data-centre group and the AI-infrastructure tape, not to GDS's own news. The dated drivers are a global tech-infrastructure selloff on 10-14 (GDS -12.8%); the Nasdaq -5.5% / SOX -12% day on 11-05 over US data-centre policy; China-tech and chip-control fears on 11-12 (-11.4%); the BIS interim final rule on 11-16 (-14.7%), which requires a licence to supply data centres serving China-headquartered firms; and reports from 10-21 that DayOne may halve or delay its US IPO. DayOne is GDS's roughly 19-20% associate, and ByteDance supplies about 69% of its revenue. The latest preview I found is Earnings Whispers on 11-18: Q3 revenue consensus about $474M, EPS $1.31 (it notes the EPS likely includes DayOne one-offs), and full-year revenue consensus about $1.84B against a raised guide of RMB12.7-13.0B (~$1.88-1.93B). The preview names the Q3 bookings pace as the deciding line: H1 was 470MW and the raised target is 1GW, so H2 needs about 530MW. Short interest was about 14.5M ADS with 6.2 days to cover on 10-30 (aggregator, snippet only). The peer VNET reported bmo on 11-23 with revenue and EBITDA roughly in line, the guide held, capex cut and a $50M buyback. It rose about 16% that day and fell about 24% the next (11-24) on margin and leverage worries. GDS moved with it, +13% on 11-23 and -7% on 11-24. The usual earnings reaction is modest: +6.2% on 2026-08-13 (Q2), and single-digit moves around the earlier prints, which I could not date exactly because EDGAR history is unavailable.
view: The stock does not trade on the China quarter. It trades on three things outside the release's own numbers: AI-infrastructure sentiment, the US export-control regime, and what the DayOne stake is worth now that DayOne's IPO is in doubt and its main customer, ByteDance, is a China-headquartered firm that the 11-16 rule now ties to licensing. The release and the 07:00 ET call can speak to all three. They should confirm a record bookings year: Alibaba's 11-19 results showed capex +60% and AI cloud +53% with demand 'accelerating', which supports the domestic line. They will likely carry another DayOne dilution gain in headline EPS. They may add capital-return or asset-recycling news, as VNET did. Management will also have to address the rule, which Alibaba itself said may lower its 20GW long-term target, and DayOne's IPO timing. They may confirm a delay or a smaller deal, and any comment on capex and leverage at 4.7x net debt/EBITDA falls in a tape that sold VNET 24% the day after a fine print. Price is 56% lower in seven weeks, tied mainly to sector and policy news. So the bar for the China numbers is low, but the external risk is still being repriced daily. The best analog, VNET, shows a same-day relief rally on an inoffensive print, and that is the nearest evidence on how this window (open to 13:00 ET) behaves. It also shows the relief does not hold in this tape. I lean slightly up, without conviction.
unpriced: Possibly a relief bounce if the domestic bookings line confirms 1GW (counterparty demand at Alibaba accelerated after GDS last spoke) and management frames DayOne's exposure to the rule as manageable. But I cannot show that the price fails to hold this. The fall came with dated policy and sector news, and the release cannot settle the policy question. No clear unpriced gap.

recommendation.reason: The China operating line will likely be fine, and the stock has fallen 56% on mostly external news, which tilts slightly toward a print-day relief move like VNET's +16% on 11-23. The deciding questions are DayOne under the 11-16 BIS rule, the IPO, and sector sentiment, and none of them can be shown as better than priced. VNET's 24% fade the next day shows the tape still sells these names. The evidence does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A clear statement that DayOne's IPO is postponed or that the ByteDance-linked capacity needs licences it may not get, or a cut to move-ins or bookings, would make it a short. A buyback, a firm 1GW-plus bookings number and a DayOne stake monetisation would make the up case clearer.

self_critique: VNET's 24% collapse today, one day after a decent print, says the market is selling the Chinese IDC group on leverage and policy whatever the numbers. GDS carries more leverage and capex than VNET, and has DayOne/ByteDance exposure that VNET lacks. The call must address the rule and the IPO, and an honest answer is more likely to disappoint than to reassure. Against that: GDS is already 2% above its 52-week low with a put skew, and a relief rally on a bmo print with a reaffirmed 1GW target is very plausible in the first three and a half hours. These roughly cancel, so 54 stays near 50.
approach_notes: P4 and P6 helped: taking the run-in apart against VNET and KWEB showed that most of the fall came with sector and policy news, and the peer's same-window reaction was the most useful evidence. P7's push to estimate the line was hard to apply where the stock trades on DayOne and export policy rather than the reported line.
